title: Europe 4 of 6 · Iberia and Mediterranean
edition: Europe countries · Six regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Europe episode four of six. First, I clear the chosen names so we can study a fresh regional group.

Our seven-place route joins Iberia with Italy and the central Mediterranean. Andorra, San Marino, Vatican City and Malta use clearly labelled supplemental maps, because the game omits these small countries.

states.name: Portugal
lines: Portugal occupies the Atlantic side of the Iberian Peninsula. Spain borders it on the north and east, while the ocean lies along its western and southern coasts.
Lisbon’s Tower of Belem commemorates Vasco da Gama’s expedition. The country’s Atlantic position helps connect that maritime history with the map.
Remember Portugal as Iberia’s western strip, facing the Atlantic. Spain is the much broader neighbour to its east.
states.transition: Let's bring Portugal and its neighbours into a closer view.

states.name: Spain
lines: Spain fills most of the Iberian Peninsula, east of Portugal and south of France across the Pyrenees. The Mediterranean follows its eastern and southeastern sides.
The Alhambra in Granada preserves the palace-and-garden world of Muslim rulers in medieval Spain. It is a vivid reminder of the long history of al-Andalus.
Picture Spain as the broad Iberian country: Portugal along the west, France beyond the northern mountains, and the Mediterranean curling along the east.

states.name: Andorra
lines: Andorra is the tiny landlocked country high in the Pyrenees between Spain and France. It belongs in the mountain gap, not on either country’s coast.
Its UNESCO-listed Madriu valley preserves mountain pastures, stone paths and traces of centuries of shared land use. The landscape tells a story of living with steep terrain.
Think Andorra in the Pyrenees: France above, Spain below, mountain communities between them. This is a labelled supplemental geographic view.

states.name: Italy
lines: Italy is the boot-shaped peninsula extending southeast from the Alps into the Mediterranean. Sicily sits near its toe, while Sardinia lies off its western side.
The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861, and Rome joined it in 1870. A familiar modern outline came together through a much more recent unification.
Use the boot, Sicily and Sardinia together. Next we will look closely at San Marino and Vatican City, two separate small states surrounded by Italy.
states.transition: Let's bring Italy and its neighbours into a closer view.

states.name: San Marino
lines: San Marino is a small inland state entirely surrounded by Italy, near the Adriatic side of the peninsula. It is separate from the Italian state around it.
Its historic centre and Mount Titano preserve a republic with roots in the Middle Ages. The towers on the mountain make a strong image for this tiny country.
Remember San Marino near Italy’s eastern side: a mountain republic inside the boot. It is not Vatican City, which sits farther southwest in Rome.

states.name: Vatican City
lines: Vatican City is the tiny independent state within Rome, entirely surrounded by Italy. We need this close supplemental view to make its outline visible.
St Peter’s Basilica, its square, palaces and gardens form an extraordinary concentration of architecture inside a very small state. The whole Vatican City is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Keep the two enclaves apart: San Marino near the Adriatic, Vatican City within Rome. Italy surrounds both, but each is a separate country.

states.name: Malta
lines: Malta is an island country south of Sicily, between the central Mediterranean’s European and North African shores. The main islands include Malta and Gozo.
Its megalithic temples preserve a prehistoric tradition of building with huge stones. The UNESCO-listed sites on Malta and Gozo make a striking contrast with the islands’ small size.
Remember Malta below Sicily: small islands, enormous ancient stones. This supplemental view completes our Iberian and central Mediterranean group.

recap: Portugal faces the Atlantic along western Iberia; Spain fills most of the peninsula, with Andorra in the Pyrenees between Spain and France.
Italy gives us the boot, Sicily and Sardinia. Keep its two enclaves separate: San Marino near the Adriatic, and Vatican City inside Rome.
Malta lies below Sicily. Think mountain valley, medieval republic, basilica and ancient stone temples: four very small states with very different locations and stories.
